chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said:

No servant ever gained a benefit better than a righteous wife. Whenever he looks at her, she delights him, and whenever he is absent from her, she preserves him — in respect to her own person and his wealth.

key_terms.حَفِظَتْهُ: she preserves/guards him — protection of both his honor and material interests in his absence
key_terms.زَوْجَةٍ صَالِحَةٍ: a righteous/pious wife — a wife who embodies taqwa, fidelity, and moral virtue
key_terms.فَائِدَةً: benefit, advantage — in Islamic ethics, worldly and spiritual gain

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about the blessing of a righteous wife?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) extols the virtue of a righteous wife as the greatest blessing a man can receive. The hadith highlights two defining qualities: her presence brings joy and comfort, and her absence prompts her to faithfully guard both her honor and his wealth. This teaching was addressed to a community for whom the household was the fundamental unit of social order, and a chaste, trustworthy wife was understood as the cornerstone of that order.
